conflicts.fact: Which lesson the cumulative model was started in and how it is described
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: initial sketch of the bicycle dynamo. Lesson 2: opens the 'cumulative model from Lesson 1 (a sketch of the Kericho generator with rotating coils near a magnet)'. Lesson 4: 'phenomenon model building since Lesson 1'. Lesson 5: model 'started in Lesson 2' (magnet, coil, galvanometer). Lesson 6: model 'building since Lesson 4'.

conflicts.fact: Strength of the induction method of magnetisation and nature of demagnetisation in the lessons
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the electrical method produces a strong electromagnet that is temporary, with stroking strongest, and that induction gives the weakest 'permanent' magnet. Lesson 1 also says soft iron is easily demagnetised, yet calls the induction magnet permanent. Lesson 2 treats the magnetised nails and rods as retaining magnetism until demagnetised.

conflicts.fact: Whether stopping a generator/dynamo is equivalent to demagnetisation, and the cause of the LED going out
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2: stopping the wheel is 'functionally equivalent to demagnetisation' and domains must stay ordered for current to flow; a stopped generator is like a demagnetised magnet. Lessons 4, 5, 6, 8: the LED goes out because relative motion stops so no flux change/cutting occurs; the magnet's domains are not affected. Lesson 7 repeats the equivalence of the bell's demagnetisation to a generator's switching.

conflicts.fact: Role of magnetisation/demagnetisation switching in generators
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 and 8 claim the bell's make-and-break magnetisation/demagnetisation is 'the same switching mechanism used in generator coils' and 'governs switching of polarity in a generator's rotating coil'. Lessons 4-6 explain generators via relative motion and flux change, with no such switching; the bell is also not an induction device.

conflicts.fact: Why the field strength/uniform field matters for induction
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says the strong constant field 'maximises the force on the moving conductor' and the coil must rotate in the field zone, while Lessons 4-5 say induced e.m.f. depends on rate of cutting flux (not a force on the conductor); the generator housing is also described as a U-shaped magnet while Lesson 4 says 'magnets (or electromagnets)'.

conflicts.fact: Name of the student and number of dynamos/turns
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 and 3 refer to an unnamed Form One student; Lesson 4 calls her Akoth; Lesson 5 calls her Amina and gives her three dynamos. Lesson 4 uses a moving straight conductor whereas Lesson 5 uses magnet pushed into a coil; Lesson 5 coil turns 20/50/100 vs predict scenario 50/200.
Lesson 5 and 8 list four factors including angle of movement; Lesson 6 lists only three (speed, number of turns, field strength).

conflicts.fact: Location where step-up transformers raise voltage
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says step-up transformers 'at Olkaria raise voltage to 132 kV' and the Lake Turkana wind farm is 310 MW; Lesson 5 says the Tana River hydroelectric generators produce thousands of volts, a non-conflicting detail; but Lesson 6 says the national grid 'depends entirely' on induction while Lesson 1's phenomenon says the generator is 'connected to the national grid line' as an input supply.
